openmp_runtime.problem: Ubuntu's libcholmod.so.5 needs GNU libgomp (GOMP_parallel, omp_get_* ; probe_gomp.log); nvc links NVIDIA's libnvomp. With both loaded the binary warns 'Another OpenMP runtime library has been detected' and aborts with 'libgomp: TODO' (runs/native_v1/stderr.txt).
openmp_runtime.settled_by: runtime library path, no rebuild of CHOLMOD and no further installation: env_run.sh, sourced by every T12 run, puts the SDK's compiler library directory first in LD_LIBRARY_PATH. The SDK ships libgomp.so.1 as a symlink to its own runtime (libgomp.so.1 -> libgomp.so -> libnvomp.so), so CHOLMOD's GOMP calls are served by libnvomp and GNU libgomp is not loaded.
openmp_runtime.source: probe_runtime.log (ldd with and without env_run.sh), runs/native_v1/stderr.txt, runs/native_patched_v1/stderr.txt

Runtime: LD_LIBRARY_PATH puts the HPC SDK's libgomp.so.1 shim first, so CHOLMOD (built against GNU libgomp) shares NVIDIA's OpenMP runtime; without it the unmodified binary warns about a second OpenMP runtime and aborts with 'libgomp: TODO' (runs/native_v1). See openmp_runtime.

Source: the five `nowait` clauses are removed (patch_nowait.diff, src_patched/): two target enter data (gpu_definitions.c), the z = u copy, the invD update from and the u += alpha p update (stencil_solvers.c). With them the binary faults with CUDA_EXCEPTION_15 'Invalid Managed Memory Access' at the kernel launch after the first nowait kernel (probe_bt.log): the device reports 'Concurrent Managed Memory: No' under WSL2 (probe_mem.log), so host access to managed memory while a deferred kernel runs is not allowed. Each of the five is followed by a taskwait before its result is used (gpu_definitions.c after the enter data; stencil_solvers.c:323 for z and invD, :389 for u), and executing a target task undeferred is one of the schedules the OpenMP standard allows for a nowait region; the patched program therefore runs one of the executions the released program permits, without the overlap.

findings.build: the released code needs three adaptations on this card and toolchain (build_adaptations): the cc89 target with Ubuntu library paths, the libgomp shim on the runtime path, and removal of its five nowait clauses because WSL2 has no concurrent managed memory
findings.stall_from_iteration_5: a result about the released code under this toolchain, not a gate failure: in the native 128x64x64 cantilever every state solve from design iteration 5 on stops at the 1000-step cap (native_iterations.csv), also with one host thread and at -O2 (runs/diag_threads1_i6, runs/diag_O2_i6); the cause was not isolated. Matched design-workload performance is left to T28.
findings.run_to_run_non_reproducibility: three harness runs with the same binary, inputs and instrumentation (harness_i5_v2, harness_i5_v3, harness_i5_v4; dumps and the two extra operator actions at states 1-5): the iteration-1 densities are bitwise equal in all three pairs, but the returned iteration-1 displacements are not bitwise equal (relative differences 3.7e-08, 3.7e-08, 3.7e-08 on the free DOFs), so the first state solve is not bitwise reproducible; the densities differ from iteration 2 on (iteration 5: max differences 4.5e-05-5.3e-05). The FP32 recursive residual of the iteration-4 solve is 7.786e-06, 7.74e-06, 7.713e-06 and that of the capped iteration-5 solve (1000 steps) is 0.9215127, 1.548609, 0.9416427. The fourth run, harness_i5, dumped only at states 1 and 5; its comparison with harness_i5_v2 (iteration-5 density difference 5.7e-05, residuals [1.507418, 0.9215127]) is kept but labelled as differently instrumented. Which operation of the first solve is nondeterministic was not located.

guards.rule: covers_process requires all six conditions: (1) every measured run is clean under t12mon.validate (vmwp found as carrier, at least 3 WDDM samples inside the job, dedicated growth within a factor 2 of the nvidia-smi device growth, shared growth under 256 MiB; with no carrier the spill state is unknown); (2) the 22 GiB control is monitored and flagged as spilled, i.e. vmwp's shared counter sees a WSL spill; (3) the live stop of monitor version 2 ends a WSL job inside WSL, before its natural end, and leaves the VM running (livestop_test_4g); (4) the repeat harness runs were admitted before launch, exited 0 with status completed, and ran clean under the live stop with checks spanning the whole job (baseline sample before launch, no gap above 5 s, a check after the exit; t12mon.record_coverage); (5) the CuPy comparison process ran under cupy_guard version 3 (lock, WSL-aware exclusivity, admission, pool cap, live stop with checks spanning the work, no allocation failure) and compare.json carries the id of the last invocation, which completed; (6) the tests of guard version 3 passed (guard_version_3_tests). Post-run detection alone does not pass the condition.

monitor_versions.1: runs native_v1, native_patched_v1, notify_i1, spill_control_22g, harness_i5, harness_i5_v2, diag_O2_i6, diag_threads1_i6: WDDM snapshots about every 2.4 s; spill evaluated only after the job exited; no admission; no live stop. Kept under the operator note on T12.
monitor_versions.2: runs livestop_test_4g, harness_i5_v3, harness_i5_v4 (and the failed first test livestop_test_4g_attempt1): admission before launch (cudaMemGetInfo inside WSL), WDDM sample about every 1.3 s with every sample after arming checked by the live stop, kill of the job's process tree inside WSL (killtree.sh), nvidia-smi on Windows and inside WSL. Defects found by the checker and fixed in version 3: it launched even when the sampler had given no baseline sample (the first sample after allocation would then have become the baseline), it waited for the job when sampling stopped mid-job, its status ignored the exit code, and its exclusivity check was not shared with the CuPy launcher and reserved nothing. Its saved runs are checked for these from their records: baseline sample before launch, checks spanning the job, exit 0 (admission_and_live_stop_per_run)
monitor_versions.3: runs livestop_v3_trigger, livestop_v3_sampler_lost, status_v3_exit3, status_v3_oom_message, contention_holder, contention_second (and the mislaunched livestop_v3_trigger_attempt1): version 2 plus the GPU lock (gpu_job.lock) and the shared exclusivity check (t12guard.exclusive_check, repeated just before launch), no launch without a baseline sample at most 5 s old, a stop when the sampler ends or gives no sample for 5 s, every checked sample time recorded (coverage), and the status from t12guard.job_status (exit code and out-of-memory messages)
monitor_versions.4: runs v4_refused_admission, v4_short_job (operator note of 2026-11-23 13:00): version 3 with coverage that fails closed (an empty or missing baseline, or no vmwp with both counters in it, refuses the launch; a sample without the watched PID or with a missing counter stops the job and marks coverage false), the watch armed before the launcher's admission probe (WSL) or CUDA context (CuPy), guard.require_budget's answer computed with no CUDA context on Windows (WSL) or in the watched process (CuPy), and a lock that an existing lock, stale or not, refuses with its owner named
monitor_versions.4.1: runs v4_1_carrier_job, v4_1_cupy_job (checker's review of version 4.0): a sample without the watched process is never a checked sample (version 4.0 counted a CuPy process's samples as checked, with zero usage, until its first appearance; negative_control_v4_0.json); cupy_guard creates the CUDA context without allocating, waits until the process appears with both counters and only then admits, caps the pool and returns for allocation; coverage of a CuPy process runs from its first appearance (LiveStop.coverage). t12mon.py: the stop action and the start of the admission probe and of the job hold one lock, the probe and the job start only when the stop has not fired, and a stop during the probe kills the probe's process tree inside WSL (probe_free.sh, killtree.sh); version 4.0 could launch after a stop that fired during its exclusivity recheck. The launcher records its steps in program order (sequence)
monitor_versions.4.2: runs v4_2_carrier_job, v4_2_trigger_job, v4_2_cupy_job (checker's review of revision 4.1): the live stop decides under the launcher's lock (LiveStop fire_lock), so the stop cannot fire between the launcher's check and the start of the probe or the job (4.1 set the stop under its own lock); the stop ends the probe and the job by one routine (t12mon.end_wsl_tree) that retries killtree.sh until the wsl.exe of the Linux process has exited, and kills that wsl.exe only as a last resort, recorded as unconfirmed (4.1 killed the probe once and then its wsl.exe, and stopped retrying the job on code 3); both launchers get the 't12job' marker as an argument before they record their PID; killtree.sh tells a PID not yet recorded (2), not a T12 job (3), not running (4) and surviving processes (5) apart; t12mon.validate credits only a carrier PID the live stop watched (carrier_is_watched) and admitted_live counts the job as covered only then; cupy_guard calls opened() once the CUDA context exists, and every sample whose Get-Counter call started after it must contain the process with both counters (the sampler records each call's start), else the job stops at once (4.1 skipped such samples for up to 10 s)

guards.carrier: WDDM 'GPU Process Memory' counters charge a WSL2 job to vmwp, not to a Linux PID. The counter covers all GPU work of the WSL VM (shared by every WSL distribution, including docker-desktop).
guards.launch_refusal: version 2 refuses to start when the WDDM counters return nothing, when another python process holds more than 200 MiB, when no WSL VM worker exists or the VM already holds more than 200 MiB (one GPU job at a time), and does not launch a job whose prediction plus 1.5 GB exceeds the free memory cudaMemGetInfo reports inside WSL. Other applications' dedicated memory is recorded, not counted (authors' decision of 2026-11-23). Version 3 takes gpu_job.lock first (the CuPy launcher too), refuses while it is held by a live process (version 4: while it exists at all, owner named), and repeats the exclusivity check immediately before launch; the CuPy launcher refuses while the WSL VM holds GPU memory. Launchers outside this folder do not take the lock; against them the check before launch is the protection, and a start between that check and the launch is not excluded.

system_match.rhs: the released FP32 load vector, widened to FP64, for every residual, compliance and solve of both codes
system_match.load: z-force, total -1, spread equally over the 4 nodes of every z=0 element face whose (i,j) index lies within radius (nely+1)/5 of (nelx, (nely-1)/2)
system_match.supports: all DOFs of the x=0 nodes with y index 0..16 and 48..64 (two strips), all z
system_match.modulus: E = 1e-6 + x^3 (1 - 1e-6), x^3 formed in FP32 as in the released elementScale; nu = 0.3
system_match.initial_iterate: zero at design iteration 1; afterwards the released loop keeps the previous U, and our matched solves start from the released U of the previous iteration

element_matrix.note: released KE: 10x10x10 midpoint rule on an edge-1 cube; nodes placed by getEdof_halo

system_match.how: our driver is given the released 24x24 element matrix (re-indexed to our node order by the node placement of getEdof_halo), the released load, supports and modulus law. Our own 2x2x2-Gauss element is not the released one: the released element is the y-mirrored element (a global sign change of the y displacements, which leaves the compliance of this z-loaded, fully clamped problem unchanged) integrated with a 10x10x10 midpoint rule, and differs from ours by 0.52% (Frobenius) after the reflection.

action_check.declared_precision: released operator: FP32 input and output vectors, FP64 element matrix and FP64 accumulation; difference expected at FP32 output rounding
action_check.reference: independent CPU FP64 element loop with the released element matrix
action_check.passed_requires: every one of the 10 actions of harness_i5_v2 and the 20 of harness_i5_v3/_v4 at or below the target, fixed rows equal to the input
action_check.states: design iterations 1-5 of harness_i5_v2; modulus contrast max/min: 1: 1, 2: 6.4e+04, 3: 2.16e+05, 4: 5.12e+05, 5: 1e+06

fp64_residual_check.definition: relative FP64 true residual of the free system ||f_f - K_ff u_f|| / ||f_f||, fixed DOFs of u set to zero, f = released FP32 load
fp64_residual_check.ours: FP64 PCG, FP32 Galerkin V-cycle (5 levels), stop on FP64 true residual 1e-5
fp64_residual_check.note: the released solver stops on its FP32 recursive residual. Where it meets that stop (design iterations 1-4) the FP64 true residual is 2.3e-04 to 5.4e-04. At iteration 5 the released solve ends at the step cap with true residual 0.92; our path, started from the same previous displacement, solves that system in 23 steps.

released_run_to_run.note: three harness runs with the same binary, inputs and instrumentation (harness_i5_v2, harness_i5_v3, harness_i5_v4; dumps and the two extra operator actions at states 1-5): the iteration-1 densities are bitwise equal in all three pairs, but the returned iteration-1 displacements are not bitwise equal (relative differences 3.7e-08, 3.7e-08, 3.7e-08 on the free DOFs), so the first state solve is not bitwise reproducible; the densities differ from iteration 2 on (iteration 5: max differences 4.5e-05-5.3e-05). The FP32 recursive residual of the iteration-4 solve is 7.786e-06, 7.74e-06, 7.713e-06 and that of the capped iteration-5 solve (1000 steps) is 0.9215127, 1.548609, 0.9416427. The fourth run, harness_i5, dumped only at states 1 and 5; its comparison with harness_i5_v2 (iteration-5 density difference 5.7e-05, residuals [1.507418, 0.9215127]) is kept but labelled as differently instrumented. Which operation of the first solve is nondeterministic was not located.

vs_compare_v3.statement: every leaf outside the timings is identical (654 of 663 common leaves equal); the 9 differing leaves are wall times of our matched and zero-start solves (wall_s_setup_excluded), which change from run to run: iteration 1, matched start, 0.3566 s in compare_v3.json and 0.0814 s now

vs_compare_v2.statement: every leaf outside the timings is identical (354 of 363 common leaves equal); the 9 differing leaves are wall times of our matched and zero-start solves (wall_s_setup_excluded), which change from run to run: iteration 1, matched start, 0.0610 s in compare_v2.json and 0.0814 s now

consequence_for_R1_1: Admitted: the fixed-state comparison on the same card and the same free-DOF system is available. The released code's native 128x64x64 run does not give a design-workload timing: on this card and toolchain its state solves stop at the step cap from design iteration 5, which is reported as a result about that code, and matched design-workload performance is left to T28. Its native stop is an FP32 recursive residual that leaves FP64 true residuals of order 1e-4 even where it is met.
